items.title: Portugal cracks down on Polymarket following suspicious election betting activity, BitRss reports
items.content_text: - **Portugal cracks down on Polymarket following suspicious election betting activity, BitRss reports** — Portugal's Gambling Regulation and Inspection Service, SRIJ, has confirmed Polymarket operates illegally in Portugal, where betting on political events is prohibited, notified the platform on Friday with 48 hours to cease activity and is moving to ask internet providers to block it. Attention followed more than 4 million euros wagered shortly before presidential results were known, with total volume on the main presidential market exceeding 120 million dollars and Antonio Jose Seguro odds surging from around 60 percent in the morning to over 90 percent by early evening ahead of official projections. ([BitRss](https://bitrss.com/portugal-cracks-down-on-polymarket-following-suspicious-election-betting-activity-174823))

items.title: Trader places 68 million dollar Bitcoin bet targeting 90,000 dollars after the US midterm vote, CoinDesk reports
items.content_text: - **Trader places 68 million dollar Bitcoin bet targeting 90,000 dollars after the US midterm vote, CoinDesk reports** — A single wallet on decentralized platform Derive bought 800 contracts of 90,000 dollar Bitcoin call options expiring on November 6, a position CoinDesk reports as approximately 68 million dollars in face value at current prices and the largest open Bitcoin position on Derive. The wallet financed the purchase in part by selling 400 contracts of 100,000 dollar calls expiring in March 2027 and another 400 contracts of 90,000 dollar calls expiring October 30, collecting about 940,000 dollars net.
